# Partner Portal Microfrontends - Project Blueprint

Version: 1.0  
Last updated: 2026-04-21

## 1. Executive Summary

This repository is a modern micro-frontend platform for a partner portal focused on risk, compliance, audit, policy, incidents, vendor risk, and partner onboarding workflows.

It replaces a legacy monolithic approach with:

- React 19 + TypeScript frontends
- Webpack 5 Module Federation (shell host + 7 remotes)
- Nx monorepo governance
- Shared libraries for auth, UI, types, API client, and eventing
- Optional containerized backend with PostgreSQL + Redis + SSE + deterministic bulk data

This document is intentionally comprehensive and reusable as a template for similar enterprise modernization programs.

## 2. Problem Context and Outcomes

### Legacy Constraints Addressed

- Tight coupling in a monolith slowed domain-specific releases.
- Inconsistent user experience across compliance and operations modules.
- Weak cross-module orchestration and limited scale testing patterns.

### Target Outcomes

- Independent domain delivery through remotely deployable frontends.
- Shared UX and security posture across all modules.
- Deterministic data generation for scale and resilience testing.
- Role-aware navigation and action-level permissions.

## 3. Platform Overview

## 3.1 Frontend Runtime Model

- Shell host runs on port 4200 and owns:
  - global layout (header, sidebar, content frame)
  - auth provider bootstrapping
  - route orchestration
  - per-remote error isolation
- 7 remote micro-apps run on ports 4201-4207 and are lazy-loaded into shell routes.

## 3.2 Backend Runtime Model

- Node/Express API service
- PostgreSQL persistence
- Redis dependency for worker-oriented flows
- Worker, publisher, and scheduler processes
- SSE stream for real-time updates
- Bulk-load endpoint for deterministic high-volume mock datasets

## 3.3 Governance Model

- Nx monorepo with affected-only operations in CI
- Shared libraries under `libs/shared`
- Import boundaries:
  - apps may depend on shared libs
  - apps must not import from other apps
  - libraries may depend on `@shared/types` (no circular dependency design)

## 5. Micro-App Catalog

| App | Port | Route | Primary Capability | Key Events |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Shell | 4200 | `/` | Host layout, routing, auth context, error boundaries | Consumes all, handles navigation events |
| Risk Assessment | 4201 | `/risk-assessment` | Risk register, scoring matrix, bulk approvals | Emits `RISK_UPDATED` |
| Compliance Dashboard | 4202 | `/compliance` | Framework scores, control status tracking | Emits `COMPLIANCE_STATUS_CHANGED` |
| Audit Management | 4203 | `/audit` | Audit plans, findings, remediation views | Emits `AUDIT_FINDING_CREATED` |
| Policy Management | 4204 | `/policy` | Policy lifecycle and approvals | Emits `POLICY_APPROVED` |
| Incident Reporting | 4205 | `/incidents` | Incident intake, timeline, investigation flow | Emits `INCIDENT_CREATED`, `INCIDENT_RESOLVED` |
| Vendor Risk | 4206 | `/vendor-risk` | Vendor registry, risk scoring, bulk assess actions | Emits `VENDOR_RISK_CHANGED` |
| Partner Onboarding | 4207 | `/onboarding` | Multi-step onboarding and bulk invite | Emits `PARTNER_ONBOARDED` |

## 6. Shared Library Contract

| Library | Responsibility | Typical Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `@shared/types` | Domain models, enums, interfaces | All apps and shared libs |
| `@shared/auth` | Auth provider, role checks, route guard | Shell and remotes |
| `@shared/ui-components` | WCAG-aligned reusable components | All remotes |
| `@shared/api-client` | Fetch wrapper + token injection + mock datasets | All remotes |
| `@shared/event-bus` | Typed cross-app pub/sub | Shell and remotes |

## 7. Security and Access Control Model

## 7.1 Authentication

- Current local mode: mock auth adapter
- Planned production mode: MSAL-backed adapter
- Token storage policy: `sessionStorage` only

## 7.2 Authorization

- Centralized permission matrix in shared auth library
- Enforced at:
  - shell navigation/menu visibility
  - app action level (create/edit/approve/etc.)

## 7.3 Navigation Safety

- Event-driven navigation is constrained to allowed root paths.
- Suspicious path forms are rejected before routing.

## 7.4 Runtime Security Controls

- Helmet-enabled backend protection
- CORS allowlist validation
- Security headers in shell static host setup
- No secrets committed in source; environment injection only

## 8. Data and Event Architecture

## 8.1 Domain Data Sources

- Local mock mode (default for frontend dev)
- Backend API mode via `API_BASE_URL`

## 8.2 Event Bus

Cross-app communication is event-driven and typed. Common events include:

- `RISK_UPDATED`
- `COMPLIANCE_STATUS_CHANGED`
- `AUDIT_FINDING_CREATED`
- `POLICY_APPROVED`
- `INCIDENT_CREATED`
- `INCIDENT_RESOLVED`
- `VENDOR_RISK_CHANGED`
- `PARTNER_ONBOARDED`
- `NAVIGATION_REQUESTED`
- `NOTIFICATION_RECEIVED`

## 8.3 Real-Time Updates

- SSE endpoint: `GET /api/events`
- Health endpoint: `GET /api/health`
- Admin stats endpoint: `GET /api/admin/stats`

## 9. Backend API and Worker Capabilities

## 9.1 Core API Patterns

- Generic domain listing and record routes:
  - `GET /api/:domain`
  - `GET /api/:domain/:id`
  - `POST /api/:domain` (mutable domains only)
  - `PATCH /api/:domain/:id`
  - `DELETE /api/:domain/:id`
- Query validation via Zod
- Domain support enforced by backend domain registry

## 9.2 Admin Operations

- Seed data: `POST /api/admin/seed`
- Deterministic bulk load: `POST /api/admin/bulk-load`
  - supports preset, seed, domain subset, and truncate toggle

## 9.3 Background Services

- `worker`
- `worker-publisher`
- `worker-scheduler`

## 12. Important Tooling Behaviors

## 12.1 Nx Wrapper

All npm scripts use `tools/scripts/run-nx.js`, which defaults to:

- `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false`
- `NX_DAEMON=false`

Reason: improves stability for some Windows environments where isolated plugin workers can fail.

## 12.2 Dev Port Preparation

`tools/scripts/prepare-dev-ports.js` frees stale repo-owned Nx listeners on ports 4200-4207 before dev startup.

Safety behavior:

- refuses to terminate processes that are not recognized as repo-owned Nx serve listeners.

## 12.3 Module Federation Runtime Isolation

For reliable route-to-remote rendering, shell and remotes should maintain explicit webpack runtime isolation fields:

- `output.uniqueName`
- `output.chunkLoadingGlobal`
- `output.hotUpdateGlobal`
- `output.devtoolNamespace`

Without this, route URLs can change while stale remote UI remains mounted.

## 13. CI/CD and Deployment

## 13.1 CI Workflow

On PRs to `main` and `develop`, and pushes to `main`:

- install via `npm ci`
- derive affected commit range via Nx SHAs action
- lint affected projects
- build affected projects
- run `npm audit --audit-level=high` (currently non-blocking)

## 13.2 Deployment Workflow

On push to `main`:

- production build for all projects
- deploy shell and each remote independently to Azure Static Web Apps using dedicated tokens

## 14. Testing Strategy

## 14.1 Frontend

- Vitest + jsdom + Testing Library
- Coverage provider: V8
- Remote module federation imports are aliased to test stubs for stable test execution

## 14.2 Backend

- Vitest + Supertest
- health and API behavior tests under backend test suite

## 14.3 Testing Guidelines

- prefer semantic queries (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`) over implementation selectors
- include accessibility checks for shared/reusable components
- keep role/permission behavior covered for critical actions

## 15. Containerized Backend Runbook

Using compose files under `deploy/docker-compose`:

- `local.base.yaml`
- `local.yaml`

Typical stack:

- postgres
- redis
- api
- worker
- worker-publisher
- worker-scheduler

Key make targets (where make is available):

- `make pm-build`
- `make pm-backend`
- `make pm-status`
- `make pm-logs`
- `make pm-bulk-load PRESET=10k SEED=42`
- `make pm-down`

If make is unavailable in the environment, run equivalent `podman compose` commands directly.

## 16. Engineering Standards

## 16.1 Code Quality

- TypeScript strict mode
- Conventional commits
- branch naming with typed prefixes (`feature/`, `bugfix/`, `docs/`, `chore/`)

## 16.2 Security

- no secrets in source control
- no token/PII logging
- input validation before API persistence
- avoid dynamic code execution patterns

## 16.3 Accessibility

- semantic HTML as default
- keyboard operability required
- visible focus indicators required
- WCAG alignment for shared components

## 16.4 Resource Efficiency

- affected-only CI tasks to reduce compute
- deterministic dataset presets for predictable load testing
- bounded bulk-load limits to avoid memory spikes

## 17. Reusable Insights for Other Projects

The following patterns are high-value and portable to other enterprise modernization programs.

## 17.1 Shell-Centered Composition Pattern

Keep layout, auth context, and routing in one host app while business domains remain independent remotes.

Benefits:

- unified UX and identity enforcement
- independent release cadence per domain team
- blast-radius reduction from per-remote error boundaries

## 17.2 Typed Event Bus over App-to-App Imports

Use strongly typed pub/sub contracts to coordinate domain updates without coupling codebases.

Benefits:

- low dependency friction
- better modularity
- easier app ownership boundaries

## 17.3 Shared Policy Matrix for RBAC

Centralize role/resource/action permissions and consume them in both navigation and action controls.

Benefits:

- consistent policy behavior
- easier audits and policy evolution

## 17.4 Deterministic Data Scaling

Implement seeded mock-generation presets (`small`, `10k`, `100k`, `600k`, `1m`, `2m`) and backend bulk-load APIs.

Benefits:

- repeatable performance tests
- realistic non-production datasets
- predictable debugging and demos

## 17.5 Safe Dev-Port Cleanup

Automate stale dev server cleanup but terminate only processes proven to belong to the current repo.

Benefits:

- fewer startup conflicts
- avoids accidental process termination outside project scope

## 17.6 CI Cost and Feedback Optimization

Use affected-only lint/build and separate deploy artifacts for each micro-app.

Benefits:

- shorter PR feedback loops
- lower CI compute cost
- independent rollback/deploy options

## 18. Extension Playbooks

## 18.1 Add a New Micro-App

1. Scaffold `apps/<new-app>` with remote entry, bootstrap, webpack config, and project config.
2. Register remote in shell federation config and route table.
3. Add role-gated nav item.
4. Add or extend permission matrix entries.
5. Add app README and tests.

## 18.2 Add a New Shared Library

1. Create library under `libs/shared/<name>`.
2. Add TS path alias in `tsconfig.base.json`.
3. Mirror alias in webpack resolve config.
4. Document public API in local README.

## 18.3 Add a New Cross-App Event

1. Add enum value and payload type in event bus.
2. Emit from source domain.
3. Subscribe in target domain(s) using the hook API.
4. Update architecture docs.

## 19. Troubleshooting Guide

## 19.1 Nx Worker Failures on Windows

Symptom:

- plugin worker startup issues during Nx command execution.

Mitigation:

- use the bundled `run-nx.js` wrapper (already wired in npm scripts)
- ensure plugin isolation and daemon are disabled where required

## 19.2 Port Conflicts

Symptom:

- `EADDRINUSE` on 4200-4207.

Mitigation:

- run `npm run dev` or `npm run start:all` so pre-start cleanup executes
- verify non-repo services are not bound to required ports

## 19.3 Remotes Not Rendering Correctly After Route Changes

Symptom:

- URL updates but stale/previous remote remains displayed.

Mitigation:

- verify webpack runtime isolation outputs are unique per app

## 19.4 Frontend Uses Mock Data Unexpectedly

Mitigation:

- set `USE_MOCK_DATA=false` and `VITE_USE_MOCKED_DATA=false`
- set API base URL explicitly
- restart frontend processes after env changes

## 19.5 Localhost Connectivity on Some Environments

If Node-side local connections fail on `localhost`, use `127.0.0.1` explicitly for backend URLs.

## 20. Forward-Looking Architecture

Planned and proposed enhancements include:

# Project Theme + Loader + Skeleton Guide

Use this document as a copy-paste starter for another web project.

## 1. Goals

- Support light and dark theme with CSS variables.
- Show a startup loader before the app mounts.
- Use skeleton loaders while data is loading.
- Keep accessibility and performance in mind.

## 2. Base index.html (Theme + Startup Loader)

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="light">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
  <title>Risk Assessment - Archaic Search Risk & Compliance</title>
  <style>
    :root {
      --color-primary: #2563eb;
      --color-danger: #dc2626;
      --color-surface: #ffffff;
      --color-bg: #f3f4f6;
      --color-text: #1f2937;
      --color-text-secondary: #6b7280;
      --color-border: #e5e7eb;
      --color-loader-track: #dbeafe;
      --color-loader-fill: #2563eb;
      --shadow-elev-1: 0 6px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08);
    }

    html[data-theme="dark"] {
      --color-primary: #60a5fa;
      --color-danger: #f87171;
      --color-surface: #111827;
      --color-bg: #030712;
      --color-text: #f3f4f6;
      --color-text-secondary: #9ca3af;
      --color-border: #374151;
      --color-loader-track: #1f2937;
      --color-loader-fill: #60a5fa;
      --shadow-elev-1: 0 8px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35);
    }

    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      html[data-theme="system"] {
        --color-primary: #60a5fa;
        --color-danger: #f87171;
        --color-surface: #111827;
        --color-bg: #030712;
        --color-text: #f3f4f6;
        --color-text-secondary: #9ca3af;
        --color-border: #374151;
        --color-loader-track: #1f2937;
        --color-loader-fill: #60a5fa;
        --shadow-elev-1: 0 8px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35);
      }
    }

    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }

    body {
      font-family: "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
      color: var(--color-text);
      background: var(--color-bg);
    }

    :focus-visible {
      outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary);
      outline-offset: 2px;
    }

    .app-loader {
      min-height: 100vh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      padding: 24px;
      background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--color-bg) 0%, var(--color-surface) 100%);
    }

    .app-loader__panel {
      width: min(440px, 92vw);
      border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
      background: var(--color-surface);
      border-radius: 14px;
      box-shadow: var(--shadow-elev-1);
      padding: 20px;
    }

    .app-loader__title {
      font-size: 1rem;
      font-weight: 700;
      margin-bottom: 8px;
    }

    .app-loader__subtitle {
      font-size: 0.9rem;
      color: var(--color-text-secondary);
      margin-bottom: 14px;
    }

    .app-loader__bar {
      width: 100%;
      height: 8px;
      border-radius: 999px;
      overflow: hidden;
      background: var(--color-loader-track);
      border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
    }

    .app-loader__fill {
      width: 40%;
      height: 100%;
      background: var(--color-loader-fill);
      border-radius: inherit;
      animation: loader-slide 1.15s ease-in-out infinite;
      transform-origin: left center;
    }

    @keyframes loader-slide {
      0% { transform: translateX(-65%); }
      50% { transform: translateX(110%); }
      100% { transform: translateX(-65%); }
    }
  </style>
  <script>
    (function initThemeEarly() {
      try {
        var saved = localStorage.getItem("theme");
        var mode = saved || "system";
        document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", mode);
      } catch (error) {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "system");
      }
    })();
  </script>
</head>
<body>
  <div id="app-loader" class="app-loader" role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-label="Loading application">
    <div class="app-loader__panel">
      <div class="app-loader__title">Archaic Search Risk & Compliance</div>
      <div class="app-loader__subtitle">Initializing application...</div>
      <div class="app-loader__bar" aria-hidden="true">
        <div class="app-loader__fill"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div id="root"></div>
</body>
</html>
```

## 3. Theme Toggle Script (Reusable)

```js
function setTheme(theme) {
  // theme: "light" | "dark" | "system"
  document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", theme);
  localStorage.setItem("theme", theme);
}

function getTheme() {
  return localStorage.getItem("theme") || "system";
}

function wireThemeToggle(buttonLight, buttonDark, buttonSystem) {
  if (buttonLight) buttonLight.addEventListener("click", function () { setTheme("light"); });
  if (buttonDark) buttonDark.addEventListener("click", function () { setTheme("dark"); });
  if (buttonSystem) buttonSystem.addEventListener("click", function () { setTheme("system"); });
}
```

## 4. Hide Loader After App Mount

### Vanilla JS

```js
function hideAppLoader() {
  var loader = document.getElementById("app-loader");
  if (!loader) return;

  loader.style.opacity = "0";
  loader.style.transition = "opacity 180ms ease";

  window.setTimeout(function () {
    loader.remove();
  }, 200);
}

// Call when app is ready
hideAppLoader();
```

### React Entry Example

```tsx
import React from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import App from "./App";

const rootElement = document.getElementById("root");
if (!rootElement) throw new Error("Root element not found");

createRoot(rootElement).render(<App />);

const loader = document.getElementById("app-loader");
if (loader) {
  loader.style.opacity = "0";
  loader.style.transition = "opacity 180ms ease";
  window.setTimeout(() => loader.remove(), 200);
}
```

## 5. Skeleton Loader CSS

```css
.skeleton {
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface) 88%, var(--color-border));
  border-radius: 8px;
}

.skeleton::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  transform: translateX(-100%);
  background: linear-gradient(
    90deg,
    transparent,
    color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary) 14%, white),
    transparent
  );
  animation: skeleton-shimmer 1.15s ease-in-out infinite;
}

@keyframes skeleton-shimmer {
  100% { transform: translateX(100%); }
}

.skeleton-text { height: 14px; }
.skeleton-text--lg { height: 22px; }
.skeleton-card { min-height: 130px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border); }
.skeleton-circle { width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 999px; }
```

## 7. React Skeleton Component Example

```tsx
import React from "react";

export function LoadingFallback() {
  return (
    <div role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-label="Loading module" style={{ display: "grid", gap: 12 }}>
      <div className="skeleton skeleton-text--lg" style={{ width: 280 }} />
      <div className="skeleton skeleton-text" style={{ width: 200 }} />

      <div style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))", gap: 10 }}>
        {Array.from({ length: 4 }).map((_, index) => (
          <div key={index} className="skeleton skeleton-card" />
        ))}
      </div>

      <div style={{ border: "1px solid var(--color-border)", borderRadius: 10, padding: 12 }}>
        {Array.from({ length: 8 }).map((_, rowIndex) => (
          <div key={rowIndex} className="skeleton" style={{ height: 30, marginBottom: 8 }} />
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## 8. Quick Integration Checklist

- Add theme tokens in :root and html[data-theme="dark"].
- Set saved theme before app boots (early script in head).
- Add startup loader container before #root.
- Remove loader after first successful render.
- Use skeleton states for tables/cards/charts while async data is loading.
- Keep role=status and aria-live=polite for accessible loading announcements.

## 9. Optional Improvements

- Replace text placeholders with shape-accurate skeletons for better perceived performance.
- Add reduced-motion support:
  - @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .skeleton::after, .app-loader__fill { animation: none; } }
- Persist theme on server for SSR apps to avoid flash between themes.
